claim: A practitioner running HA in Docker on a Raspberry Pi successfully deployed go-hass-agent v14.2.0 headless: installed the arm64 .deb, registered with a non-admin long-lived access token, and ran it without root as a systemd user service; the device appears in HA under the Mobile App integration.
stance_target: go-hass-agent is deployable headless on ARM64 Linux (e.g. Raspberry Pi) via systemd user service and registers as a mobile_app device
scope_conditions: Raspberry Pi (ARM64) with Raspberry Pi OS; HA in Docker; go-hass-agent v14.2.0
quoted_support: go-hass-agent register --token 'YOUR_TOKEN' --server http://HA_url:port/ ... systemctl --user enable go-hass-agent ... systemctl --user start go-hass-agent ... go-hass-agent must be run without root privileges, so don't use sudo to start it.
numbers: memory 27M peak 48.5M in systemd status output

claim: go-hass-agent SMART status entities appear on x86 machines (Mac mini Debian, AMD Kubuntu PC) but NOT on Raspberry Pi OS, forcing the author to build a smartctl+jq bash script, cron job and HA command_line sensor workaround to surface SMART data for the Pi.
stance_target: go-hass-agent provides uniform hardware sensor coverage across Linux platforms including ARM64 SBCs
scope_conditions: go-hass-agent v14.2.0 on Raspberry Pi OS vs Debian/Kubuntu x86; SMART disk health monitoring
quoted_support: Mac mini running Debian: SMART status is available ... Raspberry Pi running Raspberry Pi OS with Home Assistant: SMART status is not added by go-hass-agent ... While go-hass-agent exposes a wealth of system details on Raspberry Pi, it does not currently provide SMART information.

claim: go-hass-agent exposes rich SMART data as attributes on existing disk entities (e.g. Temperature_Celsius, Current_Pending_ECC_Cnt, Current_Pending_Sector) that HA template-sensor helpers must individually surface, since they are not separate entities by default.
stance_target: Consuming go-hass-agent's deep sensor data requires HA-side template helpers per attribute
scope_conditions: Home Assistant template helpers reading go-hass-agent attributes
quoted_support: go-hass-agent exposes rich SSD/HDD SMART data as attributes of the existing disk entities, including detailed health metrics that aren't shown by default.
